# `sngl dump --format sngl` prints IR back as source, so what it prints has to be
# source. Slots gave it three ways not to be: the declarations live in
# Component.Slots rather than Props, so the parameter list came out empty; a
# population lives in NodeInst.Slots rather than Children, so it vanished; and a
# component whose rest slot set ChildrenType printed both, which is refused on
# the way back in.
#
# A name written on a slot's invocation parameter is part of the contract, not a
# comment -- a slot's structural match is by name -- so the IR has to carry it
# and the dump has to print it.
#
# The check is the round trip, not the text: dump it, check the dump.

sngl dump --stage checked --format sngl slots.sngl
stdout 'header component tr.one'
stdout 'children \.\.\.component,'
stdout 'cell component\(row Row\)'

cp stdout out.sngl
sngl check out.sngl
stdout 'out.sngl: ok'

-- slots.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import tr "sngl:tree"

struct Row {
    title string
}

component table(
    rows list<Row>,
    children ...component tr.default,
    header component tr.one,
    cell component(row Row),
) {
    vbox {
        header {
            text(value="(untitled)")
        }
        for var r = rows {
            cell(r)
        }
        children
    }
}

component main {
    table(rows=[Row{title = "a"}]) {
        component header {
            text(value="Rows")
        }
        component cell(row) {
            text(value=row.title)
        }
        text(value="ordinary")
    }
}
